# `Q-9-16` — Invalid Root Element

> The root element of a CSL document is not `<style>`.

## What this means

A CSL document's root element must be `<style>` (or `<cs:style>`
when the CSL namespace is used). This error fires when the
parser reaches the root and finds something else — perhaps a
generic `<root>`, perhaps an element from a different XML
schema entirely. The message names what the parser found.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **The file is not actually a CSL document.** It parses as
  well-formed XML but follows a different schema (RSS, a
  bibliography format, a configuration file).
- **A failed download** that returned an error page (typically
  HTML) instead of the intended style file.
- **A hand-edited document** where the root element was
  renamed.

## How to fix

If the file is supposed to be a CSL style, change its root to
`<style>` (with appropriate attributes — see `Q-9-15` on
`version`). If you suspect a download problem, fetch the file
again and check that the response is XML, not an error page.

## Related

- `Q-9-5` — empty document: no root element at all.
- `Q-9-15` — invalid CSL version: a related shape error on the
  root attributes.
